+experiment_id: e19-agentic-poly-entropy-w1-qwen3-1_7b
+description: "E19: first entropy arm (E1). Token-entropy reward on top of env reward on polynomial_equations, weight 1, fork-masked to the top 20% of completion tokens by entropy (Wang 2025 forking-token motivation; note the mask restricts the reward mean, not the policy gradient). Pairs with the e12 env-only baseline (seeds 42/43). Question: does rewarding high-entropy decision points protect exploration (accuracy up, wrong/looping episodes recover) or inflate output length (Ghosal 2025)? reward_scale left at default: inert under advantage_weighted z-scoring; weight is the lever. chunk_size 1 because vLLM colocate leaves little VRAM headroom for the entropy forward pass."

+  slug: qwen3-1.7b
+  lora_r: 16
+  max_seq_length: 3072

+description: "E21: cosine length reward gets its best-case setting. The polynomial null (e9-e18) has a mechanism: correct episodes sit at the reasoning floor and the slack lives in wrong, cap-bound episodes the correctness-coupled cosine penalizes least. Watch accuracy - if compression comes at accuracy cost, that is the Wu/Yeo overshoot. Pairs with the e20 env-only control."

+experiment_id: e22-poly-cap-probe-16k
+description: "E22: cap probe, eval only, no training. Every failed episode in e9-e18 sits exactly at the 2048 completion cap (100% of wrong episodes, all arms). Whether those failures are non-terminating loops or long-but-finite reasoning was never tested - they were only ever assumed to be loops. This re-evaluates the e12 (env-only) checkpoint on the first 20 held-out seeds with a 16384 budget: if the failing episodes emit a tool call somewhere above 2048, the cap was binding and the sweep ran on truncated rollouts; if they run to 16384, they are loops and the cosine reward provably cannot shorten them (wrong-and-long is its least-penalized cell). The measured termination distribution sets the training cap and the cosine max_len for the follow-up pair. Sample index i maps to seed 100042+i, so the probe diffs sample-by-sample against the e12 report. Unlike polynomial (where correct episodes stop on their own well below the cap), countdown's correct branch is pressed against it, so the cap constrains the very episodes the cosine reward is supposed to compress. This re-evaluates the e20 (env-only) checkpoint on the first 20 held-out seeds with a 16384 budget to measure where episodes actually terminate when given room, and how many currently-failing episodes become correct. That distribution sets the training cap and the cosine max_len for the follow-up pair. Sample index i maps to seed 100042+i, so it diffs sample-by-sample against the e20 report. +experiment_id: e24-poly-4k-env-only-qwen3-1_7b
+description: "E24: control arm for the raised-cap cosine test, cosine reward off. The e22 probe showed the 2048 completion cap was the confound behind the e9-e18 null: every episode that hit the cap terminates when given room (16/16 across poly and countdown, zero loops), and on polynomial_equations all four rescued episodes are CORRECT, taking the e12 checkpoint from 0.80 to 1.00 on the same seeds. The sweep was therefore scored on rollouts cut mid-reasoning, mislabelled wrong, and then handed to the cosine wrong-branch that pays for length. Budget here is 4096 (max_seq 5120 - prompt 1024), twice the old one and the hardware ceiling on a 24 GB L4: accelerate upcasts the completion logits to fp32 for the policy backward, so peak grows by 10 bytes per token per vocab entry (bf16 logits + fp32 copy + fp32 grad, vocab 151936) on top of a 14.4 GiB resident base. Measured OOMs at 16384, 7168 and 6144 fix that model; 4096 leaves about 1.4 GiB of margin. TRL 1.6 has no chunked-logp escape (use_liger_loss does not exist in this version), and the only way past this ceiling is dropping accelerate's mixed precision, which would break numeric comparability with every earlier run. 4096 covers 18 of the 20 correct-episode lengths the probe measured - the same 18 that 6144 or 7168 would cover, because nothing in the measured distribution falls between 3093 and 9516. Pairs with e25."

+experiment_id: e25-poly-4k-cosine-w16-qwen3-1_7b
+description: "E25: the cosine length reward's fair test, paired with the e24 control. Relative to e17 (same task, same weight 16, 2048 budget, null) the completion budget doubles to 4096, which is the hardware ceiling - see e24. That takes the share of truncated-and-mislabelled rollouts from about 20 percent to about 10 percent: the e22 probe measured correct-episode lengths of median 702, p90 3093, max 9877, and 18 of 20 fit under 4096. max_len is set to 4096 as well, which here is the right call rather than the earlier design error - the error was setting max_len to a cap far above where completions actually live, because the cosine is flat near both endpoints and the whole distribution would sit in the dead zone. At a 4096 cap the covered distribution spans 213 to 3093, i.e. 5 to 75 percent of the curve, so the reward has real slope across it. With the task near-saturated at this budget most groups are all-correct, so the env component has zero within-group variance and contributes nothing under advantage_weighted, and the cosine correct-branch drives the entire gradient - the best case the countdown pair was meant to supply before the graded-scorer artifact killed its premise. Watch accuracy: compression bought with correctness is the Wu/Yeo overshoot."

content.text:
These 7 files are all pure YAML experiment configuration for a single-user research ML pipeline (thesis code, run by the researcher on their own GPU box). Each contains only hyperparameters: `experiment_id`, `seed`, model slug, LoRA rank, training mode, dataset name, reward weights, cap sizes, eval count. No entry points, no attacker-controlled inputs, no sinks — the `env_server.repo_path` and `port` are static internal values written by the researcher and consumed by their own training code, not exposed to any external principal. The `--checkpoint` paths mentioned in descriptions are documentation-only strings, not parsed by the loader.

There is no source→sink path an attacker can reach. No security-relevant findings.
